activations.domainDescription: Central dopaminergic target for reward prediction and hedonic processing
activations.domainFunction: Integrates dopamine reward signals to assign motivational value to substances and behaviors
activations.whyThisNode: Nucleus accumbens is the primary reward terminal — every addictive substance or behavior converges on NAcc dopamine release, making it the neural epicenter of addiction

treatments.label: Naltrexone (opioid antagonist)
treatments.description: Blocks opioid-mediated reward signaling in NAcc, reducing craving and heavy use days across alcohol and opioid disorders

treatments.label: Contingency management reinforcement
treatments.description: Re-trains NAcc reward circuitry by providing tangible incentives for substance-free behavior, rebuilding non-drug reward sensitivity

activations.domainDescription: Midbrain dopaminergic neurons projecting to reward and prefrontal targets
activations.domainFunction: Generates phasic and tonic dopamine signals encoding reward prediction and motivational salience
activations.whyThisNode: VTA dopamine neurons are the upstream driver of all reward signaling — chronic substance exposure alters their firing patterns, producing tolerance, sensitization, and withdrawal-driven dopamine crashes

treatments.label: Buprenorphine maintenance (partial mu-agonist)
treatments.description: Stabilizes VTA dopamine signaling in opioid use disorder by providing steady partial agonism, preventing withdrawal and blocking euphoria

treatments.label: Structured aerobic exercise program
treatments.description: Natural dopamine restoration through sustained exercise, promoting VTA neuroplastic recovery and normalizing tonic dopamine levels

activations.domainDescription: Orbitofrontal valuation system driving compulsive substance seeking
activations.domainFunction: Assigns disproportionate motivational value to substance-related stimuli, overriding negative consequences
activations.whyThisNode: OFC hyperactivation is the neural substrate of compulsive use despite harm — the hallmark of addiction as distinct from recreational use, driving behavior even when the person knows the consequences

treatments.label: CBT cognitive restructuring of craving beliefs
treatments.description: Targets OFC-mediated compulsive valuation by restructuring automatic thoughts linking substance cues to reward expectancy

treatments.label: Topiramate (glutamate/GABA modulation)
treatments.description: Reduces OFC-driven compulsive seeking through combined GABA enhancement and glutamate reduction in orbitofrontal circuits

activations.domainDescription: Prefrontal top-down control over impulsive and habitual behavior
activations.domainFunction: Provides cognitive control, working memory, and inhibitory regulation over subcortical craving signals
activations.whyThisNode: dlPFC hypofunction is universal across addiction subtypes — weakened executive control allows subcortical reward and habit circuits to dominate decision-making, producing the 'I know I shouldn't but I can't stop' experience

treatments.label: Motivational Enhancement Therapy
treatments.description: Re-engages prefrontal executive function by resolving ambivalence and strengthening intrinsic motivation through collaborative goal-setting

treatments.label: Modafinil (executive function support)
treatments.description: Glutamate and dopamine modulation improves prefrontal executive function, particularly in stimulant use disorder recovery

activations.domainDescription: Extended amygdala system mediating withdrawal distress and aversive motivation
activations.domainFunction: Generates the negative emotional states that drive continued use to avoid withdrawal, fear, and dysphoria
activations.whyThisNode: Basolateral amygdala hyperactivation underlies the 'dark side' of addiction — Koob's allostatic model shows extended amygdala recruitment converts voluntary use into compulsive avoidance of withdrawal distress

treatments.label: Gabapentin (GABAergic anxiolysis)
treatments.description: Reduces amygdala-driven withdrawal anxiety and craving through GABAergic modulation, particularly effective in high-withdrawal phenotypes

treatments.label: Trauma-focused therapy integration
treatments.description: Addresses amygdala hyperreactivity driven by unresolved trauma, which perpetuates the negative reinforcement cycle in comorbid PTSD-addiction

activations.domainDescription: Bed nucleus sustained threat monitoring driving preemptive substance use
activations.domainFunction: Maintains chronic anticipatory anxiety about withdrawal, generating the sustained dread that drives preemptive dosing
activations.whyThisNode: BNST mediates the transition from acute fear to sustained anxiety — in addiction, it generates the 'dark side' anticipatory dread that makes withdrawal feel imminent even when it is not, driving preemptive use

treatments.label: Clonidine (alpha-2 agonist)
treatments.description: Suppresses noradrenergic hyperactivity in BNST circuits, reducing anticipatory withdrawal anxiety and autonomic distress

treatments.label: Mindfulness-based relapse prevention
treatments.description: Urge surfing techniques decouple BNST anticipatory signals from behavioral responding, teaching non-reactive awareness of craving

crossDomainAffinities.role: Default Mode / Self-Referential Processing Core Operations

activations.domainDescription: Anterior insula converting bodily states into conscious craving experience
activations.domainFunction: Translates visceral and autonomic signals into the subjective experience of craving and urgency
activations.whyThisNode: Anterior insula is where craving becomes conscious — insular lesions paradoxically eliminate addiction, proving it is the critical relay converting subcortical withdrawal signals into the felt sense of 'I need a drink/hit'

treatments.label: HRV biofeedback training
treatments.description: Modulates insular interoceptive processing by training autonomic flexibility, reducing the somatic urgency component of craving

treatments.label: Interoceptive exposure during craving
treatments.description: Maps the patient's specific bodily craving signals through guided interoceptive attention, identifying somatic craving patterns for targeted intervention

activations.domainDescription: Dorsal anterior cingulate error detection and cognitive control
activations.domainFunction: Detects conflict between craving impulses and recovery goals, triggering effortful cognitive control recruitment
activations.whyThisNode: dACC is where the internal battle of addiction plays out — it monitors the conflict between wanting to use and wanting to stop, and its dysfunction explains why addicted individuals fail to recognize escalating risk patterns

treatments.label: Mindfulness meditation (conflict awareness)
treatments.description: Strengthens dACC conflict monitoring capacity through sustained attention training, improving detection of pre-lapse warning states

treatments.label: Functional assessment of use triggers
treatments.description: Maps specific internal and external triggers that overwhelm dACC conflict detection, creating a personalized relapse prevention plan

activations.domainDescription: Medial prefrontal self-referential processing maintaining addictive identity
activations.domainFunction: Sustains the self-narrative around addiction — 'I am an addict,' shame loops, and identity-level engagement with substance use
activations.whyThisNode: mPFC is the neural seat of self-concept — in addiction, it maintains the narrative identity ('I'm a drinker,' 'I can't quit') that makes substance use feel integral to who the person is, requiring identity-level intervention

treatments.label: Psilocybin-assisted identity dissolution
treatments.description: Disrupts rigid mPFC self-narrative through serotonergic-mediated ego dissolution, enabling reconstruction of identity beyond addiction

treatments.label: Narrative therapy for recovery identity
treatments.description: Actively reconstructs mPFC self-concept from 'addict' to 'person in recovery,' building a narrative that supports abstinence rather than use

activations.domainDescription: Default mode network sustaining craving-related mind-wandering and relapse ideation
activations.domainFunction: Generates spontaneous craving thoughts, past-use nostalgia, and future-use planning during unstructured mental time
activations.whyThisNode: DMN hyperactivity in addiction drives the relentless craving rumination that fills idle moments — mind-wandering becomes substance-focused, and DMN-mPFC coupling maintains the addictive self-narrative that resists recovery

treatments.label: Mindfulness-based DMN quieting
treatments.description: Meditation training reduces DMN-driven craving rumination by strengthening present-moment awareness and decentering from substance-related thought loops

treatments.label: 12-Step facilitation (narrative shift)
treatments.description: Peer support and higher-power framework provides DMN with alternative narrative content, replacing craving rumination with recovery-oriented self-referential processing

activations.domainDescription: Dorsal striatum encoding compulsive use patterns as automatic habits
activations.domainFunction: Converts voluntary substance-seeking into automated stimulus-response habits that bypass conscious decision-making
activations.whyThisNode: Striatal habit circuits are why addiction persists despite motivation to quit — Everitt and Robbins demonstrated that substance use transitions from NAcc-mediated voluntary choice to dorsal striatum-mediated automaticity, making relapse feel involuntary

treatments.label: Cue exposure and response prevention
treatments.description: Systematically decouples striatal habit associations by exposing patients to substance cues without use, extinguishing automated craving responses

treatments.label: Environmental restructuring
treatments.description: Removes or modifies the environmental cues that trigger striatal habit loops — people, places, and paraphernalia that automatically activate seeking behavior

activations.domainDescription: HPA axis stress hormone system driving stress-induced craving and relapse
activations.domainFunction: Generates cortisol and CRF signaling that converts psychosocial stress into craving, driving the stress-relapse cycle
activations.whyThisNode: HPA axis upregulation is the neuroendocrine bridge between life stress and relapse — chronic substance use produces allostatic load that elevates baseline CRF, making every stressor a potential relapse trigger

treatments.label: Cortisol reduction through aerobic exercise
treatments.description: Regular aerobic exercise normalizes HPA axis cortisol output, reducing the magnitude of stress-triggered craving responses

treatments.label: Stress inoculation training
treatments.description: Progressive stress exposure builds HPA resilience by teaching coping skills before high-stress situations arise, reducing cortisol-driven relapse

crossDomainAffinities.role: Attentional Control — Feedback & Validation — Tertiary Node

activations.domainDescription: GABAergic-glutamatergic equilibrium disrupted by chronic substance exposure
activations.domainFunction: Maintains cortical excitation-inhibition balance, profoundly disrupted by alcohol, benzodiazepines, and stimulants producing withdrawal syndromes
activations.whyThisNode: E/I balance disruption is the pharmacological core of physical dependence — chronic GABAergic substances cause compensatory glutamate upregulation, and withdrawal is the unmasked glutamate rebound producing seizures, anxiety, and excitotoxicity

treatments.label: Acamprosate (glutamate modulation)
treatments.description: Restores GABA-glutamate equilibrium post-alcohol withdrawal, reducing protracted withdrawal craving through NMDA receptor modulation

treatments.label: NAC (cystine-glutamate exchange restoration)
treatments.description: N-acetylcysteine restores extrasynaptic glutamate homeostasis in the nucleus accumbens, reducing craving across multiple substance types

activations.domainDescription: Mu/kappa/delta opioid receptor system mediating reward, pain, and social bonding
activations.domainFunction: Processes natural reward, pain modulation, and social attachment — hijacked by exogenous opioids, producing profound tolerance and dependence
activations.whyThisNode: The endogenous opioid system is directly hijacked in opioid addiction and indirectly engaged by alcohol and gambling — mu-receptor downregulation produces the hedonic deficit that makes nothing else feel good

treatments.label: Buprenorphine/naloxone maintenance
treatments.description: Partial mu-agonist stabilizes opioid receptor signaling, preventing withdrawal and blocking euphoria while allowing normal emotional function

treatments.label: Endorphin restoration through exercise
treatments.description: Sustained aerobic exercise stimulates natural endorphin release, gradually rebuilding endogenous opioid tone depleted by exogenous opioid use

activations.domainDescription: Locus coeruleus norepinephrine system generating autonomic withdrawal distress
activations.domainFunction: Produces the noradrenergic storm of acute withdrawal — sweating, tachycardia, anxiety, insomnia, hyperarousal
activations.whyThisNode: LC is the master alarm system whose unmasked hyperactivity during opioid and alcohol withdrawal produces the overwhelming autonomic distress that drives continued use — clonidine targets this specific circuit

treatments.label: Clonidine/lofexidine (alpha-2 agonist)
treatments.description: Directly suppresses LC noradrenergic firing, managing the autonomic symptoms of acute opioid and alcohol withdrawal

treatments.label: Cold exposure therapy (structured)
treatments.description: Controlled cold exposure trains healthy LC-mediated catecholamine surges, providing natural arousal as an alternative to substance-seeking

activations.domainDescription: Habenula disappointment and aversion processing in addiction
activations.domainFunction: Signals negative prediction errors and aversion, inhibiting VTA dopamine when expected rewards fail to materialize
activations.whyThisNode: Habenula hyperactivity drives the aversive 'anti-reward' state that Koob identified as central to late-stage addiction — it signals that natural rewards are disappointing compared to substance effects, deepening anhedonia

treatments.label: Behavioral activation for anhedonia
treatments.description: Gradually re-exposes the habenular anti-reward system to natural rewards, rebuilding positive prediction error signaling for non-substance activities

treatments.label: Ketamine-assisted therapy (investigational)
treatments.description: Rapid glutamatergic modulation may reset habenular hyperactivity, providing a window for behavioral intervention during the transient anti-anhedonia effect

activations.domainDescription: Ventromedial prefrontal cortex mediating fear extinction and value-based decisions
activations.domainFunction: Provides top-down inhibition of amygdala fear responses and encodes safety signals that counteract craving-associated distress
activations.whyThisNode: vmPFC hypofunction in addiction impairs fear extinction and emotional regulation — patients cannot learn that withdrawal is survivable or that craving will pass, keeping amygdala-driven negative reinforcement unchecked

treatments.label: Exposure-based craving tolerance
treatments.description: Repeated exposure to craving without use strengthens vmPFC extinction signaling, teaching the limbic system that craving is tolerable and time-limited

treatments.label: Safety planning for high-risk situations
treatments.description: Pre-planned coping responses for identified relapse triggers engage vmPFC deliberative processing before limbic craving circuits can drive automatic use

activations.domainDescription: Bidirectional gut-brain communication disrupted by substance-induced microbiome damage
activations.domainFunction: Relays inflammatory and metabolic signals from substance-damaged gut to brain, amplifying neuroinflammation, craving, and mood disturbance
activations.whyThisNode: Chronic substance use — especially alcohol and opioids — devastates the gut microbiome, increasing intestinal permeability and driving systemic inflammation that feeds back to amplify craving and impair prefrontal function

treatments.label: Probiotic microbiome restoration
treatments.description: Targeted probiotic supplementation rebuilds gut microbial diversity damaged by chronic substance use, reducing systemic inflammation and neuroinflammatory craving amplification

treatments.label: L-Glutamine gut barrier repair
treatments.description: Amino acid supplementation repairs intestinal epithelial tight junctions damaged by alcohol and opioids, reducing endotoxin translocation and neuroinflammation

crossDomainAffinities.role: Screen Reader Compatibility Human Capital & Development

activations.domainDescription: Hippocampal encoding of substance-associated contexts that trigger relapse
activations.domainFunction: Encodes powerful context-dependent memories linking specific environments, people, and situations to substance use, driving context-triggered relapse
activations.whyThisNode: Hippocampal contextual memory explains why returning to old environments triggers relapse — place cells and contextual fear conditioning create indelible substance-context associations that can reactivate craving years after abstinence

treatments.label: Memory reconsolidation disruption
treatments.description: Pharmacological or behavioral interference with substance-memory reconsolidation during retrieval can weaken hippocampal drug-context associations

treatments.label: Relapse environment mapping
treatments.description: Identifies the specific contextual cues (places, people, times, emotional states) encoded in hippocampal memory that trigger craving, enabling targeted avoidance and exposure planning

activations.domainDescription: Ventral pallidum 'liking' hotspot processing hedonic pleasure and motivation
activations.domainFunction: Encodes the hedonic 'liking' component of reward, which dissociates from 'wanting' as addiction progresses
activations.whyThisNode: Ventral pallidum contains opioid hedonic hotspots where 'liking' is generated — in addiction, VP function degrades so substances are intensely 'wanted' (NAcc) but no longer 'liked' (VP), explaining the paradox of joyless compulsive use

treatments.label: Pleasure scheduling (behavioral activation)
treatments.description: Systematic reintroduction of natural pleasures to rebuild VP hedonic capacity, counteracting the anhedonia of substance withdrawal

treatments.label: Anhedonia severity assessment
treatments.description: Quantifies the degree of hedonic deficit using validated scales, guiding medication selection and tracking recovery of natural pleasure capacity

activations.domainDescription: BDNF-mediated neuroplasticity supporting neural repair and learning in recovery
activations.domainFunction: Provides the neurotrophic support necessary for prefrontal and hippocampal recovery, enabling new learning to overwrite addictive patterns
activations.whyThisNode: BDNF is the molecular currency of recovery — exercise, therapy, and psychedelic-assisted interventions all converge on BDNF-dependent neuroplasticity to rebuild the prefrontal and hippocampal circuits degraded by chronic substance use

treatments.label: Exercise-induced BDNF elevation
treatments.description: Aerobic exercise is the most reliable BDNF elevator, directly supporting prefrontal and hippocampal neuroplastic recovery from substance-induced damage

treatments.label: Omega-3 fatty acid supplementation
treatments.description: EPA and DHA support BDNF signaling and neural membrane repair, providing the substrate for neuroplastic recovery during early abstinence

activations.domainDescription: Raphe nuclei serotonin system modulating mood, impulsivity, and craving
activations.domainFunction: Provides tonic serotonergic modulation of mood and impulse control, disrupted by multiple substances and targeted by psychedelic interventions
activations.whyThisNode: Raphe serotonin dysfunction underlies the depression, impulsivity, and mood dysregulation that both precede and perpetuate addiction — psilocybin's therapeutic mechanism works through 5-HT2A receptors originating from raphe projections

treatments.label: SSRI for comorbid depression
treatments.description: Addresses serotonergic deficits that perpetuate the depression-addiction cycle, though evidence for reducing substance use itself is mixed

treatments.label: Psilocybin-assisted serotonergic reset
treatments.description: 5-HT2A agonism produces acute neuroplastic window and mystical-type experiences associated with sustained reduction in substance use across multiple trials

activations.domainDescription: Hypothalamic regulation of sleep, appetite, and circadian rhythm disrupted by substance use
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates the homeostatic processes — sleep, appetite, temperature, circadian rhythm — that chronic substance use profoundly disrupts
activations.whyThisNode: Hypothalamic homeostatic disruption is why early recovery is physically miserable — substance-dependent resetting of sleep-wake, appetite, and temperature regulation circuits produces the physiological chaos of acute and protracted withdrawal

treatments.label: Sleep architecture reconstruction
treatments.description: Aggressive sleep hygiene protocol addressing substance-disrupted hypothalamic circadian signaling, critical for methamphetamine and alcohol recovery

treatments.label: Nutritional rehabilitation protocol
treatments.description: Structured refeeding and micronutrient repletion addressing hypothalamic appetite dysregulation and the universal nutritional depletion of active addiction

activations.domainDescription: Periaqueductal gray pain modulation hijacked by exogenous opioids
activations.domainFunction: Gates pain perception and defensive behaviors — chronic opioid exposure hijacks this circuit, producing hyperalgesia in withdrawal
activations.whyThisNode: PAG is where pain modulation meets addiction — exogenous opioids hijack the endogenous pain gate, and withdrawal unmasks opioid-induced hyperalgesia where pain sensitivity exceeds pre-addiction baseline, perpetuating use

treatments.label: Multimodal pain management plan
treatments.description: Non-opioid pain management combining physical therapy, NSAIDs, and neuromodulation to address PAG-mediated hyperalgesia without feeding the opioid cycle

treatments.label: Pain severity assessment in recovery
treatments.description: Quantifies opioid-induced hyperalgesia vs. underlying chronic pain to guide appropriate non-addictive analgesic strategies

activations.domainDescription: Ventrolateral prefrontal inhibitory control over impulsive substance seeking
activations.domainFunction: Provides the inhibitory braking that stops initial impulse from becoming action — the 'stop signal' that fails during lapse
activations.whyThisNode: vlPFC is the neural stop signal — its degradation in addiction explains the failure of inhibitory control where the person can see the consequence but cannot stop the reaching hand, making impulsivity a core circuit-level feature

treatments.label: Go/No-Go inhibitory control training
treatments.description: Computerized cognitive training targeting vlPFC inhibitory capacity, showing modest improvements in substance-related impulsivity when combined with other treatments

treatments.label: Impulsivity assessment battery
treatments.description: Quantifies inhibitory control deficits using standardized measures (BIS-11, Stop Signal Task) to identify patients requiring intensive impulse control intervention

issues.label: Alcohol Use Disorder
issues.summary: Reward circuit hijacked, habit circuit automated, executive control weakened. GABAergic/glutamatergic imbalance from chronic alcohol exposure. DMN maintains addictive identity narrative. Withdrawal is glutamate rebound plus GABAergic collapse.

_authored.detail: Nucleus accumbens reward prediction hijacked by alcohol-associated cues triggering dopamine release, driving compulsive seeking
VTA dopamine neurons adapt to chronic alcohol producing tolerance and escalation; withdrawal produces dopamine crash and anhedonia
Orbitofrontal compulsive drive overrides awareness of consequences, producing continued drinking despite clear harm
Prefrontal executive control weakened, impairing inhibition, planning, and decision-making capacity during craving
Dorsal striatum habit loop automates stimulus-craving-use-relief cycle, making drinking feel involuntary
Extended amygdala drives negative reinforcement — drinking to avoid withdrawal distress and dysphoria
Chronic alcohol enhances GABA and suppresses glutamate; withdrawal unmasks glutamate rebound causing excitotoxicity and seizure risk
CRF system upregulated creating stress-craving pathway; allostatic load drives dose escalation over time
Interoceptive craving signals — the body wants a drink; insular damage paradoxically eliminates craving
Craving-related rumination during mind-wandering increases relapse risk; meditation training reduces this
Alcohol profoundly disrupts gut microbiome, increasing intestinal permeability and driving systemic neuroinflammation

issues.label: Opioid Use Disorder
issues.summary: Endogenous opioid system hijacked. Mu-receptor tolerance drives escalating doses. Withdrawal-driven compulsion via locus coeruleus noradrenergic storm. Fentanyl supply contamination makes this the most lethal addiction.

_authored.detail: Reward system profoundly altered with mu-receptor downregulation; nothing else produces pleasure, creating hedonic allostatic shift
VTA dopamine neurons adapted to exogenous opioid input; natural rewards become insufficient to drive motivation
Locus coeruleus noradrenergic storm in withdrawal producing sweating, tachycardia, anxiety, and insomnia; clonidine target
Periaqueductal gray pain modulation hijacked by exogenous opioids producing opioid-induced hyperalgesia in withdrawal
Extended amygdala negative reinforcement drives continued use to avoid the overwhelming distress of withdrawal
Anticipatory dread of withdrawal drives preemptive dosing even when current supplies are adequate
Habit loop deeply automated: time, place, and context trigger compulsive seeking behavior
Executive control degraded with impaired decision-making persisting even in long-term abstinence
CRF system chronically elevated making every stressor a potential relapse trigger
Endogenous opioid receptor downregulation produces profound hedonic deficit and pain hypersensitivity
Identity narrative dominated by shame and self-concept as addict; DMN maintains this corrosive self-story

issues.label: Stimulant Use Disorder (Cocaine/Methamphetamine)
issues.summary: Dopamine system catastrophically depleted by chronic stimulant use. Massive dopamine release followed by profound depletion producing anhedonia, executive collapse, and compulsive redosing. No FDA-approved medication; behavioral interventions are primary.

circuits.detail: Dopamine depletion produces profound anhedonia; nothing feels good as the reward system is burned out
Dopaminergic neurons damaged by chronic stimulant exposure with slow recovery over months to years
Severe prefrontal hypofunction producing impulsivity, poor decision-making, and executive collapse
Compulsive drive persists despite devastating consequences including financial ruin and medical harm
Methamphetamine specifically neurotoxic to striatal neurons; habit loop deeply entrenched and resistant to extinction
Amygdala hyperreactive producing emotional dysregulation and paranoia, especially with methamphetamine
Interoceptive urgency signals during craving episodes drive compulsive redosing behavior
Chronic stress system activation with cortisol driving the craving-use-crash cycle
Neurotrophic signaling impaired, requiring neuroplastic support for prefrontal and hippocampal recovery
Contextual memories of use environments remain potent relapse triggers years after abstinence

issues.label: Cannabis Use Disorder
issues.summary: Endocannabinoid system downregulated by chronic exogenous THC exposure. CB1 receptor desensitization reduces natural endocannabinoid tone. Amotivational syndrome reflects prefrontal and reward circuit blunting. Withdrawal is real but non-dangerous.

_authored.detail: Reward sensitivity blunted by chronic THC-driven dopamine release; natural rewards feel insufficient
Executive function impaired with deficits in working memory, attention, and cognitive flexibility during heavy use
Hippocampal CB1 receptor density highest in brain; chronic THC impairs memory consolidation and new learning
Default mode connectivity altered producing the characteristic altered self-referential processing of chronic use
Interoceptive awareness altered; anxiety sensitivity changes drive both use and withdrawal symptoms
Amygdala CB1 modulation disrupted; paradoxical anxiety during withdrawal despite anxiolytic effects during use
Sleep and appetite regulation disrupted; insomnia and appetite loss are primary withdrawal symptoms
Motivational salience reduced; chronic use associated with amotivational state and reduced goal-directed behavior

issues.label: Nicotine Dependence
issues.summary: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor upregulation produces the fastest and most reliable addiction cycle. Rapid drug delivery (7-second lung-to-brain) creates tight stimulus-response coupling. Most commonly co-occurring substance use disorder.

_authored.detail: Nicotine directly stimulates VTA-NAcc dopamine release; 7-second delivery creates the tightest reward coupling of any substance
Nicotinic receptors on VTA neurons upregulated; withdrawal produces dopamine deficit and dysphoria
Habit loop extremely entrenched due to high-frequency daily reinforcement; 200+ puffs per day per pack
Interoceptive awareness of nicotine level drop triggers craving; smokers feel withdrawal as bodily urgency
Noradrenergic system adapted to nicotinic modulation; withdrawal irritability and concentration difficulty
Conflict monitoring disrupted; nicotine paradoxically improves attention, making cessation feel like cognitive impairment
Executive control weakened during withdrawal, reducing capacity to resist craving during cessation attempts
Contextual associations with smoking are pervasive — coffee, driving, socializing, stress all trigger hippocampal craving recall

issues.label: Gambling Disorder
issues.summary: Pure reward circuit hijacking without exogenous substance. Intermittent reinforcement schedule is maximally addictive. Same NAcc/VTA/OFC circuitry as substance addiction. Proves addiction is a circuit disorder, not a substance problem. Highest suicide rate of any addiction.

_authored.detail: Near-misses activate NAcc like actual wins; intermittent reinforcement produces maximally addictive reward schedule
Dopamine release during anticipation of uncertain reward is stronger than for certain reward, driving gambling persistence
Compulsive gambling despite financial devastation; orbitofrontal drive overrides consequence awareness
Impaired executive control producing loss-chasing, irrational probability estimation, and gambler's fallacy
Arousal signals during gambling create excitement-seeking interoceptive drive that maintains behavior
Habit loop entrenched: casino environment triggers craving triggers gambling triggers relief-excitement cycle
Risk evaluation distorted with abnormal near-miss processing driving continued play after losses
Financial stress drives cortisol which drives gambling to escape which deepens debt in a self-amplifying cycle
Gambler identity maintained by DMN; 'I can win it back' narrative sustains destructive behavior

issues.label: Benzodiazepine Dependence
issues.summary: GABAergic tolerance produces one of the most dangerous withdrawal syndromes. Compensatory glutamate upregulation creates seizure risk. Iatrogenic dependence common from prescribed use. Protracted withdrawal can persist months to years. Requires slow taper, not abrupt cessation.

_authored.detail: Chronic GABA-A receptor agonism produces downregulation and compensatory glutamate upregulation; withdrawal is excitotoxic rebound
Amygdala GABA-A receptors downregulated; withdrawal produces extreme anxiety exceeding pre-treatment baseline
Noradrenergic rebound during withdrawal producing tachycardia, tremor, sweating, and hyperarousal
Anticipatory anxiety about withdrawal drives continued use; fear of stopping becomes primary maintaining factor
Interoceptive hypervigilance during taper; patients monitor every bodily sensation as potential withdrawal symptom
Cognitive impairment during chronic use and withdrawal; working memory and executive function compromised
Emotional regulation impaired; inability to tolerate anxiety without medication perpetuates dependence
Sleep architecture disrupted; rebound insomnia during withdrawal is severe and persistent

issues.label: Polysubstance Use Disorder
issues.summary: Multiple substance dependencies creating compound circuit disruption. Each substance damages overlapping but distinct circuits, producing synergistic impairment. Treatment complexity multiplied by drug interactions, multiple withdrawal timelines, and competing pharmacological needs.

circuits.detail: dorsolateral PFC — executive working-memory / cognitive control — executive-lapse, distractible

_authored.detail: Reward system bombarded from multiple pharmacological directions; dopamine signaling chaotically dysregulated
Cumulative prefrontal damage from multiple substances produces severe executive dysfunction exceeding any single-substance effect
Excitatory-inhibitory balance disrupted by opposing substance effects; withdrawal management requires careful sequencing
Stress system maximally activated by compound withdrawal timelines and psychosocial chaos of polysubstance lifestyle
Gut microbiome devastated by multiple substance exposures; systemic inflammation drives neuroinflammatory craving amplification
Multiple habit loops entrenched; substance-switching maintains striatal activation even during partial abstinence
Amygdala hyperactivation from compound withdrawal distress; anxiety and emotional dysregulation maximally severe
Self-concept fragmented across multiple substance identities; narrative incoherence complicates identity-based recovery approaches
Endogenous opioid system disrupted by cross-substance effects; pain sensitivity and hedonic capacity both impaired
Inhibitory control severely degraded by cumulative neurotoxic exposure; impulsivity across all domains of functioning
